Nominal anvil/head and pad/fixed-cheek contacts are checked without positive-volume penetration. Moving geometry is sampled at 0–60° in 10° steps; this is not a continuous motion or post-heading axial-float proof. The three fixture pieces have no resolved fastening/clamping or load rating.

Interpretation and limits

Static source accessory at a declared tip-plane standoff, proposed saddle, and continuous bound of assumed whole-accessory rigid clocking. Final saved pin heads remain present.

Not real internal machine kinematics, heading contact, stainless qualification, axial approach or complete machine/operator access. Powerhead, custom peen, clamping hardware, force, weld distortion and OEM mounting access remain unresolved.

Early hinge setup clears the declared source-accessory/fixture geometry. Wall-attached and later-stage failures demonstrate obstructions for this saddle; they do not rule out other fixtures or processes. Accessory checks stop where a fixture collision already blocks the combined setup. No continuous axial approach or actual forming stroke is tested.

The declared whole-accessory clock bound is rotationally invariant and contains the saved source geometry; it does not establish the manufacturer's internal component motion. The 0.5 mm terminal-plane standoff deliberately does not represent contact with the pin.

See source/datum and saddle assumptions. heading_hinge_setup.step, heading_wall_setup.step and heading_cage_setup.step are static review scenes, not additional kit parts or qualified production tooling.
